patch.summary:
Thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in crm, but documented company-size audiences diverge.

Same category, different company size. Choose ACT! only if your buying job matches “ACT! by Swiftpage SMB CRM; contact sales for current packaging (no invented list prices).” rather than Salesforce's shape. Choose Salesforce only if your buying job matches “Enterprise CRM platform for sales, service, marketing, and customer data across large and ” rather than ACT!'s shape. Workflow advantage: ACT! leans contact-management; Salesforce leans sales-automation, complex-sales-processes. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in crm, but documented company-size audiences diverge.
- Positioning: ACT! is ACT! by Swiftpage SMB CRM; contact sales for current packaging (no invented list prices).; Salesforce is Enterprise CRM platform for sales, service, marketing, and customer data across large and mid-market teams..
- Company-size focus: ACT! (micro, small-business) vs Salesforce (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: ACT!-leaning contact-management vs Salesforce-leaning sales-automation, complex-sales-processes, inbound-sales.
- Researched limits: ACT! — Precise public list pricing not asserted — contact sales; Salesforce — USD list pricing rises quickly: Pro Suite $100, Enterprise $175, Unlimited $350 per user/month (annual). Add-ons (Agentforce for Sales from $125 Contact us, Revenue Intelligence, Success Plans) increase TCO..

Limitations — ACT!: Precise public list pricing not asserted — contact sales; Legacy SMB brand vs modern cloud CRM UX expectations; Salesforce: USD list pricing rises quickly: Pro Suite $100, Enterprise $175, Unlimited $350 per user/month (annual). Add-ons (Agentforce for Sales from $125 Contact us, Revenue Intelligence, Success Plans) increase TCO.; Premier Support is an add-on on Pro Suite. Agentforce for Sales, Sales Programs, Revenue Intelligence, and Revenue Cloud are separate paid add-ons; some require Contact us..

Poor-fit cases: ACT! is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Precise public list pricing not asserted — contact sales · Salesforce is a poor fit when that limitation bites: USD list pricing rises quickly: Pro Suite $100, Enterprise $175, Unlimited $350 per user/month (annual). Add-ons (Agentforce for Sales from $125 Contact us, Revenue Intelligence, Success Plans) increase TCO. · Avoid ACT! if you actually need Salesforce's motion (Enterprise CRM platform for sales, service, marketing, and customer data across )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
